newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent erases gain on technical selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent erases gain on technical selling.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil erased almost all the day's gains by the close on Monday as technical selling overcame early bullish sentiment from cold weather in Europe and northeast United States, brokers said.

December Brent closed just four cents up on the day at $23.02 per barrel, having hit a low of $22.87 minutes earlier. One broker had said a close near $23.00 was likely because of the Dec Brent options expiry on Monday.
"To some extent we are retracing the inexplicable gains of Friday," he added.
The time curve flattened slightly over the day, with February closing 10 cents up at $22.20.

Dealers said a threatened oil workers strike in Venezuela gave some support to the market, but brokers were unsure of how likely this was. The Labour Ministry called for a meeting between the Fedepetrol union and the state oil company PdVSA early this week.
Last Thursday, Fedepetrol threatened to strike in Zulia province, Venezuela's most important oil-producing region.
November gas oil had an eventful day, trading up to a high of $226.50 per tonne, before settling at $220.50, just above the day's low and 75 cents over Friday settle.
"Gas oil was pretty strong because it's freezing on both sides of the Atlantic," a broker said, adding that Tuesday's expiry of the November contract was his central concern.
Around 500,000 tonnes are expected to be delivered into the contract and whether this material can then be sold outside the region, perhaps to India, was a key question, he said.
December gas oil also gained 75 cents on the day, closing at $211.50 per tonne, but contracts further in the future climbed the most, with March 1997 up $2.50 at $196.50.
